note: Egyptian rulers for 'who was on the throne' facts. Years BC are negative numbers (-1279 is 1279 BC); years inclusive at both ends, and a reign's end year is often shared with the next reign's start year, as in the existing European lists. Egypt follows the chronology in Ian Shaw (ed.), The Oxford History of Ancient Egypt (2000), the same scheme the Karnak site files use. Alternatives differ by a few years to a few decades: Hornung, Krauss and Warburton (eds), Ancient Egyptian Chronology (2006) and von Beckerath (1997) are typically a few years different in the New Kingdom (for example Ramesses II 1279 to 1213 BC in Shaw, Hornung et al. similar, Thutmose III accession 1479 BC) but diverge more before the Middle Kingdom. Early dates (Eleventh to Seventeenth Dynasties) are approximate. Overlapping lines are simplified to the line that ruled Thebes: Twenty-first Dynasty kings at Tanis (with High Priests of Amun at Thebes), Twenty-second Dynasty (with Twenty-third and Twenty-fourth Dynasty rivals omitted), then Kushite Twenty-fifth Dynasty; co-regencies are noted in labels and the earlier king's end year is trimmed where needed. 'Rome' covers Roman emperors, then Eastern (Byzantine) emperors, as rulers of Egypt, from Augustus (30 BC) to Heraclius and the Arab conquest (AD 641 to 642); emperors are simplified in short-lived groups (Roman dates from Oxford Classical Dictionary and Britannica). 'Egypt (after the Roman period)' continues from 642 to 2026: caliphates and dynasties as periods, then Muhammad Ali's dynasty, British occupation (1882 to 1922, de facto influence to 1952) and the republic (Britannica and Oxford reference works). Dates after 2011 and for Tantawi's council are well established; check currency against 2026 if needed. Not internal or confidential material.

Egypt: Amenemhat I (Twelfth Dynasty; Senusret I co-ruler from about 1965 BC)
the Thirteenth Dynasty (many short reigns; Fourteenth Dynasty rivals in the Delta)
the Seventeenth Dynasty at Thebes (Intef kings; Hyksos Fifteenth Dynasty ruled the north)
Thutmose III (early years, under Hatshepsut's regency)
Ramesses XI (High Priests of Amun such as Herihor held Thebes in practice)
Smendes I (Twenty-first Dynasty at Tanis; High Priests of Amun at Thebes)
Takelot II (Twenty-second Dynasty; Twenty-third Dynasty rivals at Thebes)
Alexander IV (Macedonian, with Ptolemy as satrap)
Ptolemy VI Philometor (with Ptolemy VIII for part of the reign)
Ptolemy VIII Euergetes II (Physcon; brief Ptolemy VII omitted)
Cleopatra Berenice III (Ptolemy XI reigned a few weeks in 80 BC)
Cleopatra VII (with Ptolemy XIII, XIV and Caesarion)
Rome: Galba, Otho and Vitellius (Year of the Four Emperors)
Gallienus (Zenobia of Palmyra held Egypt 269 to 272)
Galerius and Maximinus Daia, then Licinius
Zeno (Eastern/Byzantine, with Leo II and Basiliscus interruptions)
Heraclius (Eastern/Byzantine; Persian occupation of Egypt 619 to 629; Arab conquest 639 to 642)
Egypt (after the Roman period): the Rashidun caliphs (Arab conquest, governor Amr ibn al-As)
the Abbasid caliphs, through governors (from Baghdad)
the Tulunid dynasty (Ahmad ibn Tulun and successors, under Abbasid overlordship)
the Abbasid governors (restored), then the Ikhshidid dynasty from 935
French occupation under Napoleon Bonaparte and successors
the Ottoman governors, with Mamluk and Albanian rivalry
Sultan, later King, Fuad I (British protectorate to 1922; kingdom with British influence)
the Supreme Council of the Armed Forces (Field Marshal Tantawi)
